claims.text: Electroless-deposited Ni or Ni–Cu coatings on W particles improve wettability with a Cu matrix during spark-plasma sintering.
Electroless-deposited Ni or Ni–Cu coatings improve interfacial bonding between W and Cu during spark-plasma sintering.
The proposed coating produces a more uniform and nearly fully dense W–Cu composite.
The proposed coating reduces void formation relative to sintered composites made from vapor-coated W powder.
The proposed coating enhances thermal transport relative to sintered composites made from vapor-coated W powder.
A uniform coating thickness of approximately 100–200 nm is suitable for the proposed intervention.
W–Cu composites containing the proposed coating can be consolidated by SPS at 800–900 °C under inert atmosphere and moderate uniaxial pressure.
The Ni interlayer acts as a chemically active bridge between W and Cu.
The Ni interlayer facilitates diffusion across the W–Cu interface.
The Ni coating lowers W–Cu interfacial energy.
The Ni coating promotes metallurgical bonding at 800–900 °C.
Enhanced interfacial diffusion minimizes void formation.
The Ni interlayer suppresses phase separation in the W–Cu composite.
Reduced void formation and suppressed phase separation improve thermal transport.
Improved interfacial bonding increases the mechanical durability of the W–Cu composite.
Interfacial defects and void formation are more pronounced in the vapor-coated W-powder baseline.
The proposed mechanism remains effective under irradiation and heat-transfer conditions typical of fusion-reactor joints.
A Ni-containing interlayer may form undesirable brittle intermetallic compounds at the W–Ni–Cu interface.
The Ni layer may alter the irradiation behavior of the W–Cu composite.

contradictions.description: The baseline asserts that vapor-coated W powders have more pronounced interfacial defects and voids, whereas the task description states that vapor-coated W powders have been sintered to achieve near-perfect contact. The hypothesis does not justify this adverse characterization of the named baseline.
